[quote=united_hydronia;59772548]They all get into the taxi. The president gives the driver the signal to go and the vehicle begins to trundle through the city. When they reach the old imperial conference hall, the president gestures for them to exit the vehicle and enter the ornately decorated building. Inside, the table is laden with typical Hydronian foods for the Dhoras to sample. It ranges from cuts of horse meat, to ice cream, to traditional bread.[/quote]

President Kourosh takes a seat and gestures for his ministers to sit with him. "Thank you for the hospitality" he says as he waits for his Hydronian hosts to start eating first, as is customary in Dhornaper.

[B]The Beginning of a Military Coup[/b]

As President Kourosh is away in Hydronia, General Fereydun Khan meets with his colonels for an upcoming military review.

He had spent several months privately and secretly persuading his colonels and some of his majors of the necessity of a coup, to overthrow a governmental system that had been keeping the country's potential back through heavy handed bureaucracy and which had been meddling incessantly in the military, slashing it's funding and introducing "oversight" committees to watch over actions of generals.

Now, he uses this pre-planned meeting as an opportunity to confirm his coup and bring alongside his officers without arousing the suspicion of the country's Directorate of Intelligence.

He sits at the head of the table and recites his grievances against the government, starting off by mentioning how his troops were underpaid and unprepared due to constant budget cuts and then listing off other objections. He then concludes that the current government isn't fit to continue ruling and they must act to set the country's course straight.

He then says that they will all have their say on whether they agree or not, with his colonels seated to his right and going around the table, descending down the hierarchy to the majors. Colonel Farrokhzhad, the first colonel and a co-conspirator, makes a show of pondering for a few moments before agreeing. To his right, Colonel Jamshid, another co-conspirator, agrees too. All four Colonels, being conspirators, agree to the coup. The first major and non-conspirator, Major Siamak, agrees. Following him, all majors agree.

With all of his assembled officers agreeing, he issues commands that they're to follow at nightfall. As most are stationed outside of the capital, they're to watch for a counter-coup and blockade any approaching loyalist forces while minimising thhe risk of escalation. Colonel Jamshid, whose forces are stationed inside the capital will be the force that decides the outcome of the coup. General Fereydun will personally command part of his forces to guarantee the coup's success.

"Embassies are no problem whatsoever. You can plan a building in the heart of Shar or we can provide an appropriate building for your embassy too" says Minister of Foreign Affairs Jalayer.

President Koroush now speaks. "As for trade. We took note of your resources and believe that there's much here to discuss. Particularly, we're interested in uranium for energy and copper for electronic components. My treasury minister will hand you a few documents that might interest you."
